title: Swag Labs catalogue navigation on a phone viewport (mobile emulation, D100)

execution.note: Real run, `npx playwright test` -> `42 passed (20.2s)`. 42 = 21 test blocks x 2 Playwright device descriptors (iPhone 13/webkit, Pixel 7/chromium); the 17 Gherkin scenarios expand to 21 blocks because 4 are Scenario Outlines. The FIRST run was 40/42: @QAIA-US-EVAL-013-004 failed on both engines because aria-hidden flips before the drawer is on screen (finding F-1, automation/traceability.md); the red run is recorded, not erased. Mobile = browser emulation only (D100); no native iOS/Android.

openArbitrations.about: the drawer breakpoint is 480/481 with 480 inclusive on the phone side -- observed, never sourced
behaviour at a fractional viewport width (480.5 px) -- unknown, deliberately not defaulted, no scenario
whether the 40x30 px sort-control stub below 900 px is an intended mobile presentation or a degradation
whether a 20x20 CSS px burger -- the sole phone navigation control -- is an accepted target size (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 sets 24x24)
the drawer has no scrim and closes only via its own control; tap-outside-to-dismiss is absent by design
whether the application reacts to an orientation change at all, or only to viewport width -- never observed, never guessed
the single-column grid holding from 320 px to 1060 px is intended, not a phone-only behaviour
the post-logout route refusal is viewport-independent, so it is asserted once rather than per device descriptor
at >=481 px with the drawer open, whether the catalogue is meant to be interactive or modal-blocked -- own measurement inconclusive at that exact width

Every mobile-specific angle in this book came from live measurement and producer initiative, not from any skill prompt.

BOOK WEAKNESS found by the real run: scenarios -006/-007/-008 assert the drawer's aria-hidden attribute, but automate's run proved aria-hidden flips to 'false' while the drawer is still fully off screen (x = -412 on a 412 px viewport). Those three scenarios would pass against a drawer that never finishes opening. The .feature was NOT edited (the human gate has not been crossed and testbook-validate is audit-only).

TESTABILITY GAP (automate step 2, reported not routed around): the drawer container .bm-menu-wrap exposes no role, no data-test and no id, yet aria-hidden -- the state AC4 asserts on -- lives on it. The page object uses a semantic CSS class, a DECLARED deviation from the role/data-testid-only rule (not positional XPath). SUT-side fix: data-test="nav-drawer" + role="dialog".
